questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two identical cylinders contain helium at 2.5 atm and argon at 1 atm respectively. If both the gases are filled in one of the cylinders, the pressure would be :
questions.solution:
Total pressure, when the two gases are filled in one cylinder is equal to sum of the pressures of the individual gases.
Thus, total pressure $=2.5+1=3.5 \mathrm{~atm}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The specific heat at constant volume for the monoatomic argon is $0.075 \mathrm{kcal} / \mathrm{kg}-\mathrm{K}$, whereas its gram molecular specific heat is $C_V=2.98 \mathrm{cal} / \mathrm{mol} \mathrm{K}$. The mass of the carbon atom is
questions.solution:
Molar specific heat
$=$ Molecular weight × gram specific heat.
$C_V=M \times C_V\begin{aligned} 2.98 \mathrm{cal} / \mathrm{mol}-\mathrm{K} & =M \times 0.075 \mathrm{kcal} / \mathrm{kg}-\mathrm{K} \\ & =\frac{M \times 0.075 \times 10^3}{10^3} \mathrm{cal} / \mathrm{g}-\mathrm{K}\end{aligned}\therefore$ Molecular weight of argon,
$M=\frac{2.98}{0.075}=39.7 \mathrm{~g}$
i.e. mass of $6.023 \times 10^{23}$ atom $=39.7 \mathrm{~g}$
Therefore, mass of
$\begin{aligned}
\text { single atom } & =\frac{39.7}{6.023 \times 10^{23}} \\
& =6.60 \times 10^{-23} \mathrm{~g}
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If one mole of a monoatomic gas $\left(\gamma=\frac{5}{3}\right)$ is mixed with one mole diatomic gas $\left(\gamma=\frac{7}{5}\right)$, the value of $\gamma$ for the mixture is
questions.solution:
For monoatomic gas,
$\gamma_1=\frac{C_{p_1}}{C_{V_1}}=\frac{5}{3}$ and $C_{p_1}-C_{V_1}=R$
this gives $C_{\rho_1}=\frac{5}{2} R$ and $C_{V_1}=\frac{3}{2} R$
For diatomic gas,
$\gamma_2=\frac{C_{\rho_2}}{C_{V_2}}=7 / 5$ and $C_{p_2}-C_{V_2}=R\Rightarrow \quad C_{P_2}=\frac{7}{2} R \quad$ and $\quad C_{V_2}=\frac{5}{2} R$
Now, we can write,
$\gamma_{\text {mix }}=\frac{n_1 C_{p_1}+n_2 C_{\rho_2}}{n_1 C_{V_1}+n_2 C_{V_2}}=\frac{C_{\rho_1}+C_{\rho_2}}{C_{V_1}+C_{V_2}}=\frac{\frac{5}{2} R+\frac{7}{2} R}{\frac{3}{2} R+\frac{5}{2} R}=\frac{12}{8}=\frac{3}{2}=1.5$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The molar specific heat of oxygen at constant pressure $C_p=7.03 \mathrm{cal} / \mathrm{mol}{ }^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ and $R=8.31 \mathrm{~J} / \mathrm{mol}^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. The amount of heat taken by 5 moles of oxygen when heated at constant volume from $10^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ to $20^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ will be approximately.
questions.solution:
Given, $C_p=7.03 \mathrm{cal} / \mathrm{mol}{ }^{\circ} \mathrm{C}, R=8.315 / \mathrm{mol}^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$,
$\begin{gathered}n=5 \text { moles, } T_2=20^{\circ} \mathrm{C}, T_1=10^{\circ} \mathrm{C}, \\ \Delta Q=?\end{gathered}\therefore$ Heat, $\Delta Q=n C_V \Delta T=n\left(C_p-R\right) \Delta T \quad\left[\because C_p-C_V=R\right]\begin{aligned} & =5\left[7.03-\frac{8.31}{4.2}\right] \times(20-10) \\ & =253 \mathrm{cal}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: 5 mol of hydrogen gas is heated from $30^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ to $60^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ at constant pressure. Heat given to the gas is (given $R=2 \mathrm{cal} / \mathrm{mol} \mathrm{deg}$ )
questions.solution:
$Q=n C_p \Delta T$
For hydrogen
$C_p=\frac{7}{2} R$
So,
$\begin{aligned} Q & =n \frac{7}{2} R \Delta T \\ & =5 \times \frac{7}{2} \times 2 \times 30 \\ & =1050 \mathrm{cal}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which of the following relation correct? ($v_{\text {rms }}$-root mean square velocity, $\bar{v}$-mean velocity and $v_{\mathrm{mp}}$-most probable velocity)
questions.solution:
The correct relation is $v_{\mathrm{rms}} \gt \bar{v} \gt v_{\mathrm{mp}}$
As $\quad \bar{v}=1.6 \sqrt{\frac{R T}{M}}, v_{\mathrm{rms}}=1.73 \sqrt{\frac{R T}{M}}$
and $\quad v_{\mathrm{mp}}=1.41 \sqrt{\frac{R T}{M}}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A diatomic gas is heated at certain pressure. What fraction of the heat energy is used to increase the internal energy?
questions.solution: $f=\frac{\Delta V}{\left(\Delta Q_p\right)}=\frac{\Delta Q_V}{\left(\Delta Q_p\right)_p}=\frac{\mu C V \Delta T}{\mu C p \Delta T}=\frac{1}{T}\begin{aligned} & f=\frac{7}{5} \\ & f=\frac{5}{7}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A mixture of two gases is contained in a vessel. The gas 1 is monoatomic and gas 2 is diatomic and the ratio of their molecular masses $M_1 / M_2=1 / 4$. What is the ratio of root mean square speeds of the molecules of two gases?
questions.solution:
From kinetic theory of gases
$p=\frac{1}{3} \frac{M}{V} \cdot e^2$
Since, $p$ and $V$ are constant (same)
$\therefore \quad M_1 e_1^2=M_2 e_2^2\Rightarrow \quad \frac{e_1^2}{e_2^2}=\frac{M_2}{M_1}\Rightarrow \quad \frac{e_1}{e_2}=\sqrt{\frac{M_2}{M_1}}=\sqrt{4 / 1}=2 \quad\left[\right.$ given, $\left.\frac{M_1}{M_2}=\frac{1}{4}\right]$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two moles of helium are mixed with $n$ moles of hydrogen. The root mean square (rms) speed of gas molecules in the mixture is $\sqrt{2}$ times the speed of sound in the mixture. Then, the value of $n$ is
questions.solution:
$\because v_{\text {mis }}=\sqrt{\frac{3 R T}{M}}$ and $v_{\text {sound }}=\sqrt{\frac{\gamma R T}{M}}$,
$v_{\mathrm{rms}}=2 v_{\text {sound }}$
i.e. $\quad \gamma=\frac{3}{2}=$ ratio of $\frac{C_p}{C_V}$ for the mixture
$C_V=\frac{n_1 C_{V_1}+n_2 C_{V_2}}{n_1+n_2}$
and
$C_p=\frac{n_1 C_{p_1}+n_2 C_{p_2}}{n_1+n_2}\therefore \quad \gamma=\frac{C_P}{C_V}=\frac{n_1 C_{p_1}+n_2 C_{p_2}}{n_1 C_{V_1}+n_2 C_{V_2}}\therefore \quad \frac{3}{2}=\frac{2\left(\frac{5}{2} R\right)+n\left(\frac{7}{2} R\right)}{2\left(\frac{3}{2} R\right)+n\left(\frac{5}{2} R\right)}\begin{array}{ll}\Rightarrow & \frac{3}{2}=\frac{10+7 n}{6+5 n} \\ \Rightarrow & n=2\end{array}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If the rms velocity of a gas is $v$, then
questions.solution:
Rms velocity is given by
$v=\sqrt{\frac{3 k T}{m}} \text { or } v^2=\frac{3 k T}{m}$
For a gas, $k$ and $m$ are constants.
$\therefore \frac{v^2}{T}=\text { constant }$
